ESV.1: Ah, you destroyer, who yourself have not been destroyed, you traitor, whom none has betrayed! When you have ceased to destroy, you will be destroyed; and when you have finished betraying, they will betray you.
ESV.2: O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be our arm every morning, our salvation in the time of trouble.
ESV.3: At the tumultuous noise peoples flee; when you lift yourself up, nations are scattered,
ESV.4: and your spoil is gathered as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts leap, it is leapt upon.
ESV.5: The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he will fill Zion with justice and righteousness,
ESV.6: and he will be the stability of your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is Zion's  treasure.
ESV.7: Behold, their heroes cry in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
ESV.8: The highways lie waste; the traveler ceases. Covenants are broken; cities  are despised; there is no regard for man.
ESV.9: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is confounded and withers away; Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
ESV.10: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD, “now I will lift myself up; now I will be exalted.
ESV.11: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble; your breath is a fire that will consume you.
ESV.12: And the peoples will be as if burned to lime, like thorns cut down, that are burned in the fire.”
ESV.13: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might.
ESV.14: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling has seized the godless: “Who among us can dwell with the consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?”
ESV.15: He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, who despises the gain of oppressions, who shakes his hands, lest they hold a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes from looking on evil,
ESV.16: he will dwell on the heights; his place of defense will be the fortresses of rocks; his bread will be given him; his water will be sure.
ESV.17: Your eyes will behold the king in his beauty; they will see a land that stretches afar.
ESV.18: Your heart will muse on the terror: “Where is he who counted, where is he who weighed the tribute? Where is he who counted the towers?”
ESV.19: You will see no more the insolent people, the people of an obscure speech that you cannot comprehend, stammering in a tongue that you cannot understand.
ESV.20: Behold Zion, the city of our appointed feasts! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, an untroubled habitation, an immovable tent, whose stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
ESV.21: But there the LORD in majesty will be for us a place of broad rivers and streams, where no galley with oars can go, nor majestic ship can pass.
ESV.22: For the LORD is our judge; the LORD is our lawgiver; the LORD is our king; he will save us.
ESV.23: Your cords hang loose; they cannot hold the mast firm in its place or keep the sail spread out. Then prey and spoil in abundance will be divided; even the lame will take the prey.
ESV.24: And no inhabitant will say, “I am sick”; the people who dwell there will be forgiven their iniquity.

NASB.1: Woe to you, O destroyer, While you were not destroyed; And he who is treacherous, while [others] did not deal treacherously with him. As soon as you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; As soon as you cease to deal treacherously, [others] will deal treacherously with you.
NASB.2: O LORD, be gracious to us; we have waited for You. Be their strength every morning, Our salvation also in the time of distress.
NASB.3: At the sound of the tumult peoples flee; At the lifting up of Yourself nations disperse.
NASB.4: Your spoil is gathered [as] the caterpillar gathers; As locusts rushing about men rush about on it.
NASB.5: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
NASB.6: And He will be the stability of your times, A wealth of salvation, wisdom and knowledge; The fear of the LORD is his treasure.
NASB.7: Behold, their brave men cry in the streets, The ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
NASB.8: The highways are desolate, the traveler has ceased, He has broken the covenant, he has despised the cities, He has no regard for man.
NASB.9: The land mourns [and] pines away, Lebanon is shamed [and] withers; Sharon is like a desert plain, And Bashan and Carmel lose [their foliage].
NASB.10: 'Now I will arise,' says the LORD, 'Now I will be exalted, now I will be lifted up.
NASB.11: 'You have conceived chaff, you will give birth to stubble; My breath will consume you like a fire.
NASB.12: 'The peoples will be burned to lime, Like cut thorns which are burned in the fire.
NASB.13: 'You who are far away, hear what I have done; And you who are near, acknowledge My might.'
NASB.14: Sinners in Zion are terrified; Trembling has seized the godless. 'Who among us can live with the consuming fire? Who among us can live with continual burning?'
NASB.15: He who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity, He who rejects unjust gain And shakes his hands so that they hold no bribe; He who stops his ears from hearing about bloodshed And shuts his eyes from looking upon evil;
NASB.16: He will dwell on the heights, His refuge will be the impregnable rock; His bread will be given [him], His water will be sure.
NASB.17: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty; They will behold a far-distant land.
NASB.18: Your heart will meditate on terror: 'Where is he who counts? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?'
NASB.19: You will no longer see a fierce people, A people of unintelligible speech which no one comprehends, Of a stammering tongue which no one understands.
NASB.20: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; Your eyes will see Jerusalem, an undisturbed habitation, A tent which will not be folded; Its stakes will never be pulled up, Nor any of its cords be torn apart.
NASB.21: But there the majestic [One], the LORD, will be for us A place of rivers [and] wide canals On which no boat with oars will go, And on which no mighty ship will pass--
NASB.22: For the LORD is our judge, The LORD is our lawgiver, The LORD is our king; He will save us--
NASB.23: Your tackle hangs slack; It cannot hold the base of its mast firmly, Nor spread out the sail. Then the prey of an abundant spoil will be divided; The lame will take the plunder.
NASB.24: And no resident will say, 'I am sick'; The people who dwell there will be forgiven [their] iniquity.

NKJV.1: Woe to you who plunder, though you have not been plundered; And you who deal treacherously, though they have not dealt treacherously with you! When you cease plundering, You will be plundered; When you make an end of dealing treacherously, They will deal treacherously with you.
NKJV.2: O LORD, be gracious to us;  We have waited for You. Be their arm every morning, Our salvation also in the time of trouble.
NKJV.3: At the noise of the tumult the people shall flee; When You lift Yourself up, the nations shall be scattered;
NKJV.4: And Your plunder shall be gathered Like the gathering of the caterpillar; As the running to and fro of locusts, He shall run upon them.
NKJV.5: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
NKJV.6: Wisdom and knowledge will be the stability of your times, And the strength of salvation; The fear of the LORD is His treasure.
NKJV.7: Surely their valiant ones shall cry outside,  The ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly.
NKJV.8: The highways lie waste, The traveling man ceases.  He has broken the covenant, He has despised the cities, He regards no man.
NKJV.9: The earth mourns and languishes, Lebanon is shamed and shriveled; Sharon is like a wilderness, And Bashan and Carmel shake off their fruits.
NKJV.10: “Now  I will rise,” says the LORD; “Now I will be exalted, Now I will lift Myself up.
NKJV.11: You shall conceive chaff, You shall bring forth stubble; Your breath, as fire, shall devour you.
NKJV.12: And the people shall be like the burnings of lime; Like thorns cut up they shall be burned in the fire.
NKJV.13: Hear, you who are afar off, what I have done; And you who are near, acknowledge My might.”
NKJV.14: The sinners in Zion are afraid; Fearfulness has seized the hypocrites: “Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? Who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?”
NKJV.15: He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, He who despises the gain of oppressions, Who gestures with his hands, refusing bribes, Who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed, And shuts his eyes from seeing evil:
NKJV.16: He will dwell on high; His place of defense will be the fortress of rocks; Bread will be given him, His water will be sure.
NKJV.17: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty; They will see the land that is very far off.
NKJV.18: Your heart will meditate on terror: “Where is the scribe? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?”
NKJV.19: You will not see a fierce people, A people of obscure speech, beyond perception, Of a stammering tongue that you cannot understand.
NKJV.20: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet home, A tabernacle that will not be taken down; Not one of its stakes will ever be removed, Nor will any of its cords be broken.
NKJV.21: But there the majestic LORD will be for us A place of broad rivers and streams, In which no galley with oars will sail, Nor majestic ships pass by
NKJV.22: (For the LORD is our Judge, The LORD is our Lawgiver, The LORD is our King; He will save us);
NKJV.23: Your tackle is loosed, They could not strengthen their mast, They could not spread the sail. Then the prey of great plunder is divided; The lame take the prey.
NKJV.24: And the inhabitant will not say, “I am sick”; The people who dwell in it will be forgiven their iniquity.

AMP.1:
Woe (judgment is coming) to you, O destroyer,
You who were not destroyed,
And he who is treacherous, while others did not deal treacherously with him.
As soon as you finish destroying, you will be destroyed;
As soon as you stop dealing treacherously, others will deal treacherously with you.
AMP.2:
O LORD, be gracious to us; we have waited [expectantly] for You.
Be the arm of Your servants every morning [that is, their strength and their defense],
Our salvation also in the time of trouble.
AMP.3:
At the sound of the tumult, the peoples flee;
At the lifting up of Yourself nations scatter.
AMP.4:
Your spoil [of Israel's foe] is gathered [by the people of Jerusalem] as the caterpillar gathers;
As locusts swarming so people swarm on it.
AMP.5:
The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high;
He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
AMP.6:
And He will be the security and stability of your times,
A treasure of salvation, wisdom and knowledge;
The fear of the LORD is your treasure.
AMP.7:
Now look, their brave men shout outside;
The ambassadors [seeking a treaty] of peace weep bitterly.
AMP.8:
The highways are deserted, the traveler has ceased [to appear].
The enemy has broken the covenant, he has rejected the cities,
He has no regard for [any] man.
AMP.9:
The land mourns and dries out,
Lebanon is shamed and [its lush foliage] withers;
Sharon is like a desert plain,
And Bashan and [Mount] Carmel shake off their leaves.
AMP.10:
"Now I will arise," says the LORD.
"Now I will be exalted; now I will be lifted up.
AMP.11:
"You have conceived dried grass, you will give birth to stubble;
My breath is a fire that will consume you.
AMP.12:
"The peoples will be burned to lime,
Like thorns cut down which are burned in the fire.
AMP.13:
"You who are far away, hear what I have done;
And you who are near, acknowledge My might."
AMP.14:
The sinners in Zion are terrified;
Trembling has seized the godless.
[They cry] "Who among us can live with the consuming fire?
Who among us can live with everlasting burning?"
AMP.15:
He who walks righteously and speaks with integrity,
Who rejects gain from fraud and from oppression,
Who shakes his hand free from the taking of bribes,
Who stops his ears from hearing about bloodshed
And shuts his eyes to avoid looking upon evil;
AMP.16:
He will dwell on the heights,
His place of defense will be the fortress of rocks,
His bread will be given him;
His water will be permanent.
AMP.17:
Your eyes will see the King in His beauty;
They will see a far-distant land.
AMP.18:
Your mind will meditate on the terror [asking]:
"Where is he who counts?
Where is he who weighs [the tribute]?
Where is he who counts the towers?"
AMP.19:
You will no longer see the fierce and insolent people,
A people of unintelligible speech which no one comprehends,
Of a strange and stammering tongue which no one understands.
AMP.20:
Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts and observances;
Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a undisturbed settlement,
A tent which will not be taken down;
Not one of its stakes will ever be pulled up,
Nor any of its ropes be severed.
AMP.21:
But there the mighty and magnificent LORD will be for us
A place of broad rivers and streams,
Where no oar-driven boat will go,
And on which no mighty and stately ship will pass.
AMP.22:
For the LORD is our Judge,
The LORD is our Ruler,
The LORD is our King;
He will save us.
AMP.23:
Your ship's ropes (tackle) hang loose;
They cannot hold the base of their mast firmly,
Nor spread out the sail.
Then an abundance of spoil and plunder will be divided;
Even the lame will take the plunder.
AMP.24:
And no inhabitant [of Zion] will say, "I am sick";
The people who dwell there will be forgiven their wickedness [their sin, their injustice, their wrongdoing].

WEB.1: Woe to you who destroy, but you weren’t destroyed; and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have finished betrayal, you will be betrayed.
WEB.2: Yahweh, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
WEB.3: At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled. When you lift yourself up, the nations are scattered.
WEB.4: Your plunder will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.
WEB.5: Yahweh is exalted, for he dwells on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
WEB.6: There will be stability in your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of Yahweh is your treasure.
WEB.7: Behold, their valiant ones cry outside; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
WEB.8: The highways are desolate. The traveling man ceases. The covenant is broken. He has despised the cities. He doesn’t respect man.
WEB.9: The land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is confounded and withers away. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.
WEB.10: “Now I will arise,” says Yahweh; “Now I will lift myself up. Now I will be exalted.
WEB.11: You will conceive chaff. You will give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will devour you.
WEB.12: The peoples will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.
WEB.13: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and, you who are near, acknowledge my might.”
WEB.14: The sinners in Zion are afraid. Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?
WEB.15: He who walks righteously, and speaks blamelessly; He who despises the gain of oppressions, who gestures with his hands, refusing to take a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from looking at evil —
WEB.16: he will dwell on high. His place of defense will be the fortress of rocks. His bread will be supplied. His waters will be sure.
WEB.17: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty. They will see a distant land.
WEB.18: Your heart will meditate on the terror. Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers?
WEB.19: You will no longer see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that you can’t comprehend, with a strange language that you can’t understand.
WEB.20: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that won’t be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
WEB.21: But there Yahweh will be with us in majesty, a place of wide rivers and streams, in which no galley with oars will go, neither will any gallant ship pass by there.
WEB.22: For Yahweh is our judge. Yahweh is our lawgiver. Yahweh is our king. He will save us.
WEB.23: Your rigging is untied. They couldn’t strengthen the foot of their mast. They couldn’t spread the sail. Then the prey of a great plunder was divided. The lame took the prey.
WEB.24: The inhabitant won’t say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell therein will be forgiven their iniquity.

NLT.1:
What sorrow awaits you Assyrians, who have destroyed others
but have never been destroyed yourselves.
You betray others,
but you have never been betrayed.
When you are done destroying,
you will be destroyed.
When you are done betraying,
you will be betrayed.
NLT.2:
But LORD, be merciful to us,
for we have waited for you.
Be our strong arm each day
and our salvation in times of trouble.
NLT.3:
The enemy runs at the sound of your voice.
When you stand up, the nations flee!
NLT.4:
Just as caterpillars and locusts strip the fields and vines,
so the fallen army of Assyria will be stripped!
NLT.5:
Though the LORD is very great and lives in heaven,
he will make Jerusalem his home of justice and righteousness.
NLT.6:
In that day he will be your sure foundation,
providing a rich store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge.
The fear of the LORD will be your treasure.
NLT.7:
But now your brave warriors weep in public.
Your ambassadors of peace cry in bitter disappointment.
NLT.8:
Your roads are deserted;
no one travels them anymore.
The Assyrians have broken their peace treaty
and care nothing for the promises they made before witnesses.
They have no respect for anyone.
NLT.9:
The land of Israel wilts in mourning.
Lebanon withers with shame.
The plain of Sharon is now a wilderness.
Bashan and Carmel have been plundered.
NLT.10:
But the LORD says: “Now I will stand up.
Now I will show my power and might.
NLT.11:
You Assyrians produce nothing but dry grass and stubble.
Your own breath will turn to fire and consume you.
NLT.12:
Your people will be burned up completely,
like thornbushes cut down and tossed in a fire.
NLT.13:
Listen to what I have done, you nations far away!
And you that are near, acknowledge my might!”
NLT.14:
The sinners in Jerusalem shake with fear.
Terror seizes the godless.
“Who can live with this devouring fire?” they cry.
“Who can survive this all-consuming fire?”
NLT.15:
Those who are honest and fair,
who refuse to profit by fraud,
who stay far away from bribes,
who refuse to listen to those who plot murder,
who shut their eyes to all enticement to do wrong —
NLT.16:
these are the ones who will dwell on high.
The rocks of the mountains will be their fortress.
Food will be supplied to them,
and they will have water in abundance.
NLT.17:
Your eyes will see the king in all his splendor,
and you will see a land that stretches into the distance.
NLT.18:
You will think back to this time of terror, asking,
“Where are the Assyrian officers
who counted our towers?
Where are the bookkeepers
who recorded the plunder taken from our fallen city?”
NLT.19:
You will no longer see these fierce, violent people
with their strange, unknown language.
NLT.20:
Instead, you will see Zion as a place of holy festivals.
You will see Jerusalem, a city quiet and secure.
It will be like a tent whose ropes are taut
and whose stakes are firmly fixed.
NLT.21:
The LORD will be our Mighty One.
He will be like a wide river of protection
that no enemy can cross,
that no enemy ship can sail upon.
NLT.22:
For the LORD is our judge,
our lawgiver, and our king.
He will care for us and save us.
NLT.23:
The enemies’ sails hang loose
on broken masts with useless tackle.
Their treasure will be divided by the people of God.
Even the lame will take their share!
NLT.24:
The people of Israel will no longer say,
“We are sick and helpless,”
for the LORD will forgive their sins.

MSG.1:
Doom to you, Destroyer,
not yet destroyed;
And doom to you, Betrayer,
not yet betrayed.
When you finish destroying,
your turn will come—destroyed!
When you quit betraying,
your turn will come—betrayed!
MSG.2:
God, treat us kindly. You're our only hope.
First thing in the morning, be there for us!
When things go bad, help us out!
MSG.3:
You spoke in thunder and everyone ran.
You showed up and nations scattered.
MSG.4:
Your people, for a change, got in on the loot,
picking the field clean of the enemy spoils.
MSG.5:
God is supremely esteemed. His center holds.
Zion brims over with all that is just and right.
MSG.6:
God keeps your days stable and secure—
salvation, wisdom, and knowledge in surplus,
and best of all, Zion's treasure, Fear-of-God.
MSG.7:
But look! Listen!
Tough men weep openly.
Peacemaking diplomats are in bitter tears.
MSG.8:
The roads are empty—
not a soul out on the streets.
The peace treaty is broken,
its conditions violated,
its signers reviled.
MSG.9:
The very ground under our feet mourns,
the Lebanon mountains hang their heads,
Flowering Sharon is a weed-choked gully,
and the forests of Bashan and Carmel? Bare branches.
MSG.10:
"Now I'm stepping in," God says.
"From now on, I'm taking over.
The gloves come off. Now see how mighty I am.
MSG.11:
There's nothing to you.
Pregnant with chaff, you produce straw babies;
full of hot air, you self-destruct.
MSG.12:
You're good for nothing but fertilizer and fuel.
Earth to earth—and the sooner the better.
MSG.13:
"If you're far away,
get the reports on what I've done,
And if you're in the neighborhood,
pay attention to my record.
MSG.14:
The sinners in Zion are rightly terrified;
the godless are at their wit's end:
'Who among us can survive this firestorm?
Who of us can get out of this purge with our lives?' "
MSG.15:
The answer's simple:
Live right,
speak the truth,
despise exploitation,
refuse bribes,
reject violence,
avoid evil amusements.
MSG.16:
This is how you raise your standard of living!
A safe and stable way to live.
A nourishing, satisfying way to live.
MSG.17:
Oh, you'll see the king—a beautiful sight!
And you'll take in the wide vistas of land.
MSG.18:
In your mind you'll go over the old terrors:
"What happened to that Assyrian inspector who condemned and confiscated?
And the one who gouged us of taxes?
And that cheating moneychanger?"
MSG.19:
Gone! Out of sight forever! Their insolence
nothing now but a fading stain on the carpet!
No more putting up with a language you can't understand,
no more sounds of gibberish in your ears.
MSG.20:
Just take a look at Zion, will you?
Centering our worship in festival feasts!
Feast your eyes on Jerusalem,
a quiet and permanent place to live.
No more pulling up stakes and moving on,
no more patched-together lean-tos.
MSG.21:
Instead, God! God majestic, God himself the place
in a country of broad rivers and streams,
But rivers blocked to invading ships,
off-limits to predatory pirates.
MSG.22:
For God makes all the decisions here. God is our king.
God runs this place and he'll keep us safe.
MSG.23:
Ha! Your sails are in shreds,
your mast wobbling,
your hold leaking.
The plunder is free for the taking, free for all—
for weak and strong, insiders and outsiders.
MSG.24:
No one in Zion will say, "I'm sick."
Best of all, they'll all live guilt-free.

NIV.1:
Distress and Help
Woe to you, O destroyer,
you who have not been destroyed!
Woe to you, O traitor,
you who have not been betrayed!
When you stop destroying,
you will be destroyed;
when you stop betraying,
you will be betrayed.
NIV.2:
O Lord, be gracious to us;
we long for you.
Be our strength every morning,
our salvation in time of distress.
NIV.3:
At the thunder of your voice, the peoples flee;
when you rise up, the nations scatter.
NIV.4:
Your plunder, O nations, is harvested as by young locusts;
like a swarm of locusts men pounce on it.
NIV.5:
The Lord is exalted, for he dwells on high;
he will fill Zion with justice and righteousness.
NIV.6:
He will be the sure foundation for your times,
a rich store of salvation and wisdom and knowledge;
the fear of the Lord is the key to this treasure.
NIV.7:
Look, their brave men cry aloud in the streets;
the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
NIV.8:
The highways are deserted,
no travelers are on the roads.
The treaty is broken,
its witnesses are despised,
no one is respected.
NIV.9:
The land mourns and wastes away,
Lebanon is ashamed and withers;
Sharon is like the Arabah,
and Bashan and Carmel drop their leaves.
NIV.10:
“Now will I arise,” says the Lord.
“Now will I be exalted;
now will I be lifted up.
NIV.11:
You conceive chaff,
you give birth to straw;
your breath is a fire that consumes you.
NIV.12:
The peoples will be burned as if to lime;
like cut thornbushes they will be set ablaze.”
NIV.13:
You who are far away, hear what I have done;
you who are near, acknowledge my power!
NIV.14:
The sinners in Zion are terrified;
trembling grips the godless:
“Who of us can dwell with the consuming fire?
Who of us can dwell with everlasting burning?”
NIV.15:
He who walks righteously
and speaks what is right,
who rejects gain from extortion
and keeps his hand from accepting bribes,
who stops his ears against plots of murder
and shuts his eyes against contemplating evil—
NIV.16:
this is the man who will dwell on the heights,
whose refuge will be the mountain fortress.
His bread will be supplied,
and water will not fail him.
NIV.17:
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty
and view a land that stretches afar.
NIV.18:
In your thoughts you will ponder the former terror:
“Where is that chief officer?
Where is the one who took the revenue?
Where is the officer in charge of the towers?”
NIV.19:
You will see those arrogant people no more,
those people of an obscure speech,
with their strange, incomprehensible tongue.
NIV.20:
Look upon Zion, the city of our festivals;
your eyes will see Jerusalem,
a peaceful abode, a tent that will not be moved;
its stakes will never be pulled up,
nor any of its ropes broken.
NIV.21:
There the Lord will be our Mighty One.
It will be like a place of broad rivers and streams.
No galley with oars will ride them,
no mighty ship will sail them.
NIV.22:
For the Lord is our judge,
the Lord is our lawgiver,
the Lord is our king;
it is he who will save us.
NIV.23:
Your rigging hangs loose:
The mast is not held secure,
the sail is not spread.
Then an abundance of spoils will be divided
and even the lame will carry off plunder.
NIV.24:
No one living in Zion will say, “I am ill”;
and the sins of those who dwell there will be forgiven.

NRSVCE.1:

who yourself have not been destroyed;
you treacherous one,
with whom no one has dealt treacherously!
When you have ceased to destroy,
you will be destroyed;
and when you have stopped dealing treacherously,
you will be dealt with treacherously.
NRSVCE.2:
O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you.
Be our arm every morning,
our salvation in the time of trouble.
NRSVCE.3:
At the sound of tumult, peoples fled;

NRSVCE.4:
Spoil was gathered as the caterpillar gathers;

NRSVCE.5:
The LORD is exalted, he dwells on high;
he filled Zion with justice and righteousness;
NRSVCE.6:
he will be the stability of your times,

NRSVCE.7:
Listen! the valiant cry in the streets;

NRSVCE.9:
The land mourns and languishes;

NRSVCE.10:
“Now I will arise,” says the LORD,

now I will be exalted.
NRSVCE.11:

NRSVCE.13:

NRSVCE.14:

NRSVCE.15:
Those who walk righteously and speak uprightly,
who despise the gain of oppression,
who wave away a bribe instead of accepting it,

and shut their eyes from looking on evil,

they will live on the heights;

NRSVCE.17:
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty;

NRSVCE.18:

NRSVCE.19:
No longer will you see the insolent people,
the people of an obscure speech that you cannot comprehend,
stammering in a language that you cannot understand.
NRSVCE.20:
Look on Zion, the city of our appointed festivals!
Your eyes will see Jerusalem,
a quiet habitation, an immovable tent,
whose stakes will never be pulled up,
and none of whose ropes will be broken.
NRSVCE.21:
But there the LORD in majesty will be for us
a place of broad rivers and streams,
where no galley with oars can go,

NRSVCE.22:
For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our ruler,

NRSVCE.23:
Your rigging hangs loose;

NRSVCE.24:
And no inhabitant will say, “I am sick”;
the people who live there will be forgiven their iniquity.

NET.1: The destroyer is as good as dead, you who have not been destroyed! The deceitful one is as good as dead, the one whom others have not deceived! When you are through destroying, you will be destroyed; when you finish deceiving, others will deceive you!
NET.2: LORD, be merciful to us! We wait for you. Give us strength each morning! Deliver us when distress comes.
NET.3: The nations run away when they hear a loud noise; the nations scatter when you spring into action!
NET.4: Your plunder disappears as if locusts were eating it; they swarm over it like locusts!
NET.5: The LORD is exalted, indeed, he lives in heaven; he fills Zion with justice and fairness.
NET.6: He is your constant source of stability; he abundantly provides safety and great wisdom; he gives all this to those who fear him.
NET.7: Look, ambassadors cry out in the streets; messengers sent to make peace weep bitterly.
NET.8: Highways are empty, there are no travelers. Treaties are broken, witnesses are despised, human life is treated with disrespect.
NET.9: The land dries up and withers away; the forest of Lebanon shrivels up and decays. Sharon is like the desert; Bashan and Carmel are parched.
NET.10: “Now I will rise up,” says the LORD. “Now I will exalt myself; now I will magnify myself.
NET.11: You conceive straw, you give birth to chaff; your breath is a fire that destroys you.
NET.12: The nations will be burned to ashes; like thorn bushes that have been cut down, they will be set on fire.
NET.13: You who are far away, listen to what I have done! You who are close by, recognize my strength!”
NET.14: Sinners are afraid in Zion; panic grips the godless. They say, ‘Who among us can coexist with destructive fire? Who among us can coexist with unquenchable fire?’
NET.15: The one who lives uprightly and speaks honestly; the one who refuses to profit from oppressive measures and rejects a bribe; the one who does not plot violent crimes and does not seek to harm others —
NET.16: This is the person who will live in a secure place; he will find safety in the rocky, mountain strongholds; he will have food and a constant supply of water.
NET.17: You will see a king in his splendor; you will see a wide land.
NET.18: Your mind will recall the terror you experienced, and you will ask yourselves, “Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighs the money? Where is the one who counts the towers?”
NET.19: You will no longer see a defiant people whose language you do not comprehend, whose derisive speech you do not understand.
NET.20: Look at Zion, the city where we hold religious festivals! You will see Jerusalem, a peaceful settlement, a tent that stays put; its stakes will never be pulled up; none of its ropes will snap in two.
NET.21: Instead the LORD will rule there as our mighty king. Rivers and wide streams will flow through it; no war galley will enter; no large ships will sail through.
NET.22: For the LORD, our ruler, the LORD, our commander, the LORD, our king — he will deliver us.
NET.23: Though at this time your ropes are slack, the mast is not secured, and the sail is not unfurled, at that time you will divide up a great quantity of loot; even the lame will drag off plunder.
NET.24: No resident of Zion will say, “I am ill”; the people who live there will have their sin forgiven.
